164.h: 69 - ʿIyāḍ ibn Ghanm ibn Zuhayr ibn Abī Shaddād Abū Saʿd al-Fihrī *
164.t:
He was among those who gave the Pledge of al-Riḍwān, and his kinsman Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ appointed him as successor over Syria when he was on his deathbed (1) .
Narrating from him: جبير بن نفير، وغيره.
He was good, righteous, an ascetic (الزاهد), generous, and it was he who conquered al-Jazīrah by treaty.
ʿUmar confirmed him over Syria, and he lived some two years after that.
It is said: he lived sixty years, and died in the year 20 in Syria (2) .
Ibn Saʿd said: He witnessed al-Ḥudaybiyah, and was one of the five commanders on the day of al-Yarmūk (3) . ⟦2:354⟧
Narrating from him: عياض بن عمرو الأشعري.
I say: As for ʿIyāḍ ibn Zuhayr al-Fihrī, he was a great Badrī (البدري), and he is the paternal uncle of ʿIyāḍ ibn Ghanm, also known by the patronymic (الكنية) Abū Saʿd; he has no transmission; he died in the time of ʿUthmān in the year 30 (may Allah be pleased with them both).

165.h: 70 - Salamah ibn Salāmah ibn Waqsh ibn Zaghbah al-Ashhalī *
165.t:
Ibn Zaʿūrāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Ashhal, Abū ʿAwf al-Ashhalī, the cousin (the son of the paternal aunt) of Muḥammad ibn Maslamah.
He witnessed: the two ʿAqabahs, Badr, Uḥud, and the battles (1) .
He has a hadith in (Musnad al-Imām Aḥmad) from the narration of Maḥmūd ibn Labīd, from him (2) . ⟦2:355⟧
It is said: he died in the year 34.
Ibn Saʿd said: He died in the year 45, aged 70, and was buried in Medina, and his line has died out (1) .
The Prophet ﷺ paired him in brotherhood with Abū Sibrah ibn Abī Ruhm al-ʿĀmirī.
It is said: between him and al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām.

166.h: 71 - al-Nuʿmān ibn Muqarrin Abū Ḥakīm al-Muzanī *
166.t:
It is said: Abū ʿAmr al-Muzanī, the commander, Companion (الصحابي) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ⟦2:356⟧
The banner of his people was in his charge on the day of the conquest of Mecca, then he was commander of the army that conquered Nahāwand (1) , and he was martyred that day (2) .
His prayers were answered, and ʿUmar announced his death to the Muslims from the pulpit, and wept.
Narrating from him: ابنه؛ معاوية، ومعقل بن يسار، ومسلم بن الهيضم، وجبير بن حية الثقفي.
He was killed in the year 21, on a Friday (may Allah be pleased with him) (3) .
زائدة: حدثنا عاصم بن كليب الجرمي، حدثني أبي:
That news of Nahāwand and Ibn Muqarrin was slow to reach ʿUmar, and that he was praying for victory, and that the people, because of what they saw of his praying for victory, had no concern except Nahāwand and Ibn Muqarrin.
Then a Bedouin emigrant came to them, and when he reached al-Baqīʿ, he said: What news has come to you of Nahāwand?
They said: And what is that?
He said: Nothing.
So ʿUmar sent for him, and he came to him and said: I was coming with my family as an emigrant until we reached such-and-such a place, and when we turned back, there was a rider on a red camel, the like of which I had never seen, and I said: O servant of Allah! Where have you come from?
He said: From Iraq.
I said: What is the news of the people?
He said: The people fought at Nahāwand, and Allah gave victory over it, and Ibn Muqarrin was killed; by Allah, I do not know which of the people he is, nor what Nahāwand is.
He said: Do you know which day of the week that was?
He said: No.
ʿUmar said: But I know; count your stopping places.
He said: We stopped at such-and-such a place, then set out, and stopped at such-and-such a stopping place, until he had counted.
ʿUmar said: That was such-and-such a day of the week; perhaps you met a courier from among the couriers of the jinn, for they have couriers. ⟦2:357⟧
He waited what he waited, then the bearer of good news came that they had met on that day (1) .
The sons of ʿAfrāʾ:

167.h: 72 - Muʿādh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Rifāʿah al-Anṣārī *
167.t:
Ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Sawād ibn Mālik ibn Ghanm ibn Mālik ibn al-Najjār al-Anṣārī, al-Najjārī.
Brother of: ʿAwf, Rāfiʿ, and Rifāʿah.
Their mother: ʿAfrāʾ bint ʿUbayd ibn Thaʿlabah ibn ʿUbayd ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Ghanm ibn Mālik ibn al-Najjār.
He witnessed Badr.
His children were: ʿUbayd Allāh, al-Ḥārith, ʿAwf, Salmā, Ibrāhīm, ʿĀʾishah, and Sārah.
al-Wāqidī said: It is narrated that this Muʿādh and Rāfiʿ ibn Mālik al-Zuraqī were the first of the Anṣār to accept Islam in Mecca, and the account of the six is better established (2) .
Muʿādh witnessed both ʿAqabahs.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ paired him in brotherhood with Maʿmar ibn al-Ḥārith al-Jumaḥī, one of the Badrīs (البدري) (3) . ⟦2:358⟧
Muʿādh died after the killing of ʿUthmān, and he has descendants (1) .

168.h: 73 - Muʿawwidh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Rifāʿah al-Anṣārī *
168.t:
Ibn ʿAfrāʾ; he is the father of al-Rubayyiʿ bint Muʿawwidh, and of her sister ʿUmayrah.
He witnessed al-ʿAqabah with the seventy, according to Ibn Isḥāq alone.
He is the one of whom it was said: that he struck Abū Jahl, he and his brother ʿAwf, until they had disabled him. Then he turned upon them and killed them, then he fell down prostrate, then he was finished off (2) by Ibn Masʿūd.
Muʿawwidh and ʿAwf (3) had stood that day in the line beside ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, and they said to him:
O uncle, do you know Abū Jahl? We have been told that he harms the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
So he pointed him out to them, and the two of them charged at him together.

169.h: 74 - ʿAwf ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Rifāʿah al-Anṣārī **
169.t:
Ibn ʿAfrāʾ. ⟦2:359⟧
He witnessed al-ʿAqabah.
Some of them counted him as one of the six men who first met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (1) .
He witnessed Badr and was martyred.
And their fourth brother:

170.h: 75 - Rifāʿah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Rifāʿah al-Anṣārī *
170.t:
A Badrī (البدري).
Ibn Isḥāq alone mentioned him.
al-Wāqidī said: That is not firmly reliable (ثبت) with us.
ʿAwf has descendants.
Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim said: I heard Ibn Sīrīn say regarding the killing of Abū Jahl:
The two sons of ʿAfrāʾ struck him down, and Ibn Masʿūd finished him off (2) .
And in the narration of: صالح بن إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف، عن أبيه، عن جده:
That the two who asked him, and killed Abū Jahl, were: Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ; and Muʿādh ibn ʿAfrāʾ (3) , and this is more correct. ⟦2:360⟧

171.h: 76 - Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān ibn Jābir al-ʿAbsī * (ع)
171.t:
Among the distinguished Companions (الصحابي) of Muḥammad ﷺ, and he was the keeper of the secret (1) .
The name of al-Yamān was: Ḥisl - and it is said: Ḥusayl - ibn Jābir al-ʿAbsī, al-Yamānī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh, an ally of the Anṣār, one of the notables of the Emigrants.
Narrating from him: أبو وائل؛ وزر بن حبيش، وزيد بن وهب، وربعي بن حراش، وصلة بن زفر، وثعلبة بن زهدم، وأبو العالية الرياحي، وعبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، ومسلم بن نذير، وأبو إدريس الخولاني، وقيس بن عباد، وأبو البختري الطائي، ونعيم بن أبي هند، وهمام بن الحارث؛ وخلق سواهم.
He has in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين): twelve hadiths, and in al-Bukhārī: eight, and in Muslim: seventeen hadiths. ⟦2:361⟧
His father Ḥisl had shed blood among his people, so he fled to Medina and made an alliance with Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal, and his people called him al-Yamān, because of his alliance with the Yamānīs, who are the Anṣār (1) .
He and his son Ḥudhayfah witnessed Uḥud, and he was martyred that day, killed by some of the Companions (الصحابي) by mistake, not recognising him, because armies conceal themselves in their war armour and cover their faces; and if they have no clear mark, a brother may sometimes kill his brother without realising.
When they charged at al-Yamān that day, Ḥudhayfah kept shouting: My father! My father! O people! But it was done in error, so Ḥudhayfah gave his blood-money (الدية) in charity to them (2) .
al-Wāqidī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ paired Ḥudhayfah and ʿAmmār in brotherhood.
And so said Ibn Isḥāq.
إسرائيل: عن أبي (3) إسحاق، عن رجل، عن حذيفة: that he came, he ⟦2:362⟧ and his father, and Abū Jahl met them. He said: Where to?
They said: A need of ours.
He said: You have come only to reinforce Muḥammad.
So they took a firm pledge from the two of them that they would not add to the numbers against them, and they came to the Messenger of Allah and informed him (1) .
ابن جريج: أخبرني أبو حرب بن أبي الأسود، عن أبي الأسود؛ قال:
وعن رجل، عن زاذان:
That ʿAlī was asked about Ḥudhayfah, and he said: He knew the hypocrites, and asked about the difficult matters; if you ask him, you will find him knowledgeable of them (2) .
أبو عوانة: عن سليمان، عن ثابت أبي المقدام، عن أبي يحيى، قال:
A man asked Ḥudhayfah - and I was with him - saying: What is hypocrisy?
He said: That you speak of Islam, and do not act by it.
Sallām ibn Miskīn, from Ibn Sīrīn:
That ʿUmar wrote in the appointment of Ḥudhayfah over al-Madāʾin: Listen to him, and obey, and give him what he asks of you.
So he left ʿUmar's presence on a saddled donkey, with his provisions beneath him, and when he arrived, the dihqāns met him, while in his hand was a loaf of bread and a bone with some meat (3) . ⟦2:363⟧
Ḥudhayfah was made governor of al-Madāʾin by ʿUmar, and remained over it until after the killing of ʿUthmān, and he died forty nights after ʿUthmān.
Ḥudhayfah said: What prevented me from witnessing Badr was only that I went out with my father, and the disbelievers of Quraysh seized us, and they said: You want Muḥammad!
We said: We want only Medina.
So they took a pledge from us: that we would return to Medina, and not fight with him.
We informed the Prophet ﷺ and he said: (We will keep faith with their pledge, and seek Allah's help against them (1)) .
The Prophet ﷺ had confided to Ḥudhayfah the names of the hypocrites, and he retained from him the tribulations that would occur in the Community (2) .
ʿUmar had adjured him: Am I among the hypocrites?
He said: No, and I will not vouch for anyone after you (3) .
And Ḥudhayfah: he is the one whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dispatched on the night of al-Aḥzāb to gather news of the enemy for him (4) , and at his hand al-Dīnawar (5) was conquered by force.
His virtues are many (may Allah be pleased with him).
أبو إسحاق: عن مسلم بن نذير، عن حذيفة، قال: the Prophet ﷺ ⟦2:364⟧ took hold of the muscle of my calf, and said: (The wearing of the lower garment is here; if you refuse, then lower; if you refuse, then the lower garment has no right in what is below the ankles.)
In another wording: (The lower garment has no right at the ankles (1)) .
عقيل، ويونس: عن الزهري، أخبرني أبو إدريس، سمع حذيفة يقول:
By Allah, I am the most knowledgeable of people about every tribulation that will occur between me and the Hour (2)) .
Ḥudhayfah said: The people used to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about good, and I used to ask him about evil, fearing that it would overtake me (3) .
الأعمش: عن أبي وائل، عن حذيفة، قال:
The Messenger of Allah stood among us in a standing, and told us of everything that would be until the rising of the Hour; whoever memorised it memorised it, and whoever forgot it forgot it (4) . ⟦2:365⟧
I say: He ﷺ used to recite his speech slowly and explain it; perhaps in that sitting he said what would be written in a hadith fascicle (الجزء); so he mentioned the greatest of the coming events, and had he mentioned most of what is to be in existence, he could not have said it in a year, indeed not even in years, so ponder this.
Ḥudhayfah died: in al-Madāʾin, in the year 36, having grown old.
Ibn Sīrīn said: ʿUmar sent Ḥudhayfah to al-Madāʾin, and he read his appointment to them.
They said: Ask whatever you wish.
He said: Food that I may eat, and fodder for this donkey of mine - as long as I am among you - of straw.
He stayed among them as long as Allah willed; then ʿUmar wrote to him: Come.
When news of his coming reached ʿUmar, he hid for him on the road; and when he saw him in the same state in which he had set out, he came to him, embraced him, and said: You are my brother, and I am your brother (1) .
Mālik ibn Mighwal, from Ṭalḥah:
Ḥudhayfah came to al-Madāʾin on a donkey, letting his legs hang down, with a bone and a loaf in his hand (2) .
Saʿīd ibn Masrūq al-Thawrī, from ʿIkrimah: This is the riding of the prophets, letting the legs hang down on one side.
Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh: I heard Abū Isḥāq say:
Ḥudhayfah used to come every Friday from al-Madāʾin to Kufa.
Abū Bakr said: I said to him: Is this possible?
He said: He had a swift, sturdy mule.
ابن سعد: أخبرنا محمد بن عبد الله الأسدي، حدثنا عبد الجبار بن ⟦2:366⟧ العباس، عن أبي عاصم الغطفاني، قال:
Ḥudhayfah would continually relate a hadith that they found shocking.
It was said to him: You are about to tell us that there will be metamorphosis among us!
He said: Yes! There will surely be metamorphosis among you: apes and pigs.
Abū Wāʾil, from Ḥudhayfah, said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Write down for me those among the people who utter Islam.)
So we wrote down for him: one thousand five hundred (1) .
سفيان: عن الأعمش، عن موسى بن عبد الله بن يزيد، عن أمه، قالت:
In Ḥudhayfah's ring were two cranes, between them: Praise be to Allah (2) .
عيسى بن يونس: عن الأعمش، عن موسى، عن أمه، قالت:
Ḥudhayfah's ring was of gold, with a sky-blue ruby stone; on it were two cranes facing each other; between them: Praise be to Allah (3) .
حماد بن سلمة: أخبرنا علي بن زيد، عن الحسن، عن جندب:
That ⟦2:367⟧ Ḥudhayfah said: There is no speech I speak by which twenty lashes would be warded off from me but that I would speak it.
خالد: عن أبي قلابة، عن حذيفة، قال:
I buy my religion, part of it with part, fearing that all of it will go (1) .
أبو نعيم: حدثنا سعد بن أوس، عن بلال بن يحيى، قال:
It reached me that Ḥudhayfah used to say: No one of the Companions (الصحابي) lived to see this matter except that he had bought part of his religion with part.
They said: And you?
He said: And I, by Allah: I go in to one of them - and there is no one but has in him good qualities and bad - and I mention his good qualities and turn away from the rest, and sometimes one of them invites me to lunch, and I say: I am fasting, and I am not fasting.
A group, from al-Ḥasan, said:
When death came to Ḥudhayfah, he said: A beloved has come in need; one who regrets does not prosper! Is there not after me what I know! Praise be to Allah who made me precede the tribulation! Its leaders and its brutes (2) .
شعبة: أخبرنا عبد الملك بن ميسرة، عن النزال بن سبرة، قال:
I said to Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī: What did Ḥudhayfah say at his death?
He said: When it was near dawn, he said: I seek refuge in Allah from a morning that leads to the Fire - three times - then said: Buy me two white garments; for they will not be left on me except a little, until I am given better than them in exchange, or they are stripped from me, a foul stripping. ⟦2:368⟧
شعبة أيضا: عن أبي إسحاق، عن صلة بن زفر، عن حذيفة، قال:
Buy me a shroud.
They brought a robe worth three hundred, and he said: No, buy me two white garments.
And from Jazy ibn Bukayr, he said:
When ʿUthmān was killed, we turned in alarm to Ḥudhayfah, and went in to him.
Ibn Saʿd said: Ḥudhayfah died in al-Madāʾin, after ʿUthmān (1) , and has descendants.
His brother Ṣafwān ibn al-Yamān also witnessed Uḥud.

172.h: 77 - Muḥammad ibn Maslamah ibn Salamah ibn Khālid al-Anṣārī * (ع)
172.t:
Ibn ʿAdī ibn Majdaʿah, Abū ʿAbd Allāh - and it is said: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and Abū Saʿīd - al-Anṣārī, al-Awsī.
One of the distinguished Companions (الصحابي); he witnessed: Badr, and the battles.
It is said that the Prophet ﷺ once appointed him as deputy over Medina.
He (may Allah be pleased with him) was among those who withdrew from the tribulation, and was present neither at the Camel nor at Ṣiffīn; rather he made a sword of wood, and moved to al-Rabadhah, and stayed there for a short while (2) . ⟦2:369⟧
A group narrated hadiths.
Narrating from him: المسور بن مخرمة، وسهل بن أبي حثمة، وقبيصة بن ذؤيب، وعبد الرحمن الأعرج، وعروة بن الزبير، وأبو بردة بن أبي موسى، وابنه؛ محمود بن محمد.
He was of Banū Ḥārithah, among the allies of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal.
He was a tall man, dark-skinned, of medium build, bald, dignified.
ʿUmar had appointed him over the zakat of Juhaynah.
When a complaint was made to ʿUmar about an official, he would send Muḥammad to them to investigate his affair.
He left behind of children: ten sons; and six daughters (may Allah be pleased with him).
It is said: the name of his grandfather was Khālid ibn ʿAdī ibn Majdaʿah.
He came to al-Jābiyah, and was in the vanguard of ʿUmar's army.
عباد بن موسى السعدي: حدثنا يونس، عن الحسن، عن محمد بن مسلمة، قال:
I passed by, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on al-Ṣafā, placing his hand on the hand of a man, so I went on.
He said: (What prevented you from giving greeting?)
I said: O Messenger of Allah! You did something with this man that you did with no one, so I disliked to interrupt your conversation; who was he, O Messenger of Allah?
He said: (Jibrīl, and he said to me: This is Muḥammad ibn Maslamah, he did not give greeting; but had he given greeting, we would have returned the greeting to him.)
I said: And what did he say to you, O Messenger of Allah?
He said: (He kept advising me about the neighbour, until I thought he would command me to make him an heir) (1) . ⟦2:370⟧
Ibn Saʿd said: Muḥammad ibn Maslamah accepted Islam at the hand of Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr, before the conversion of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh.
He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ paired him in brotherhood with Abū ʿUbaydah, and appointed him deputy over Medina in the year of Tabūk (1) .
حماد بن سلمة: عن ابن جدعان، عن أبي بردة، قال:
We passed by al-Rabadhah, and there was the tent of Muḥammad ibn Maslamah, and I said: Would that you went out to the people, and commanded and forbade?
He said: The Prophet ﷺ said to me: (O Muḥammad, there will be division, and tribulation, and disagreement, so break your sword, cut your bowstring, and sit in your house.)
And I did what he commanded me (2) .
شعبة: عن أشعث، عن أبي بردة، عن ضبيعة (3) :
Ḥudhayfah said: I know a man whom tribulation will not harm.
He said: And there was a tent when we came to Medina, and there was Muḥammad ibn Maslamah (4) .
Ibn Yūnus said: Muḥammad witnessed the conquest of Egypt, and was among those who climbed the fortress with al-Zubayr.
ʿAbāyah ibn Rifāʿah said: Muḥammad ibn Maslamah was dark, tall, and large. ⟦2:371⟧
And in the authentic (الصحيح) collections, from the hadith of Jābir: the killing of Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf at the hand of Muḥammad ibn Maslamah (1) .
ابن المبارك: أخبرنا ابن عيينة، عن موسى بن أبي عيسى، قال:
ʿUmar came to the upper room (2) of Banū Ḥārithah, and found Muḥammad ibn Maslamah, and said: O Muḥammad, how do you see me?
He said: I see you as I love, and as one who wishes you well would love, strong in gathering wealth, abstinent from it, just in distributing it, and if you inclined, we would set you straight, as the arrow is straightened in the straightening-frame.
He said: Praise be to Allah who put me among a people who, if I incline, set me straight (3) .
ابن عيينة: عن عمرو بن سعيد، عن أبيه، عن عباية بن رفاعة، قال:
It reached ʿUmar that Saʿd had built a palace, and said: The little voice has been cut off.
So ʿUmar sent Muḥammad ibn Maslamah - and when ʿUmar liked a matter to be brought as he wished, he would send him - and he came to Kufa, kindled a fire, and burned the door on Saʿd.
He came to Saʿd and said: It reached ʿUmar that you said: The little voice has been cut off.
So he swore that he had not said it (4) .
هشام: عن ابن سيرين، عن حذيفة، قال:
There is no one for whom I do not fear tribulation except Muḥammad ibn Maslamah, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (Tribulation will not harm him) (5) . ⟦2:372⟧
al-Fasawī in his (Tārīkh): حدثنا محمد بن مصفى، حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد، عن موسى بن وردان، عن أبيه، عن جابر، قال:
Muʿāwiyah came with the people of Syria with him, and what Muḥammad ibn Maslamah had done - his sitting out from ʿAlī and Muʿāwiyah - reached a wretched man of the people of the Jordan, so he burst into his house and killed him.
Then Muʿāwiyah sent to Kaʿb ibn Mālik: What do you say about Muḥammad ibn Maslamah (1) ?
Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr, Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Numayr, Shabāb, and a group said:
Muḥammad ibn Maslamah died in Ṣafar, in the year 43 (2) .
يزيد بن هارون: أخبرنا هشام، عن الحسن:
That the Prophet ﷺ gave Muḥammad ibn Maslamah a sword and said: (Fight the polytheists with it, and when you see the Muslims turning on one another, strike Uḥud with it until you break it, then sit in your house until a sinful hand comes to you, or a deadly fate (3)) .
Something similar is also narrated from the mursal (مرسل) reports of Zayd ibn Aslam.
Ibn Maslamah lived seventy-seven years. ⟦2:373⟧

173.h: 78 - ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Thaqafī * (م، 4)
173.t:
The commander, the virtuous, the trustworthy, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Thaqafī, al-Ṭāʾifī.
He came in the delegation of Thaqīf to the Prophet ﷺ in the year 9, and they accepted Islam, and he appointed him over them when he saw his intellect and his eagerness for good and religion, and he was the youngest of the delegation in age (1) .
Then Abū Bakr confirmed him over al-Ṭāʾif, then ʿUmar, then ʿUmar appointed him over ʿUmān and Bahrain, then sent him ahead with an army, and he conquered Tawwaj and its principal city, and settled in Basra (2) . ⟦2:374⟧
al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī mentioned him and said: I have seen no one better than him.
I say: He has hadiths in (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (1)) , and in the Sunan collections (السنن).
His mother had witnessed the birth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Narrating from him: سعيد بن المسيب، ونافع بن جبير بن مطعم، ويزيد ومطرف ابنا عبد الله بن الشخير، وموسى بن طلحة، وآخرون.
سالم بن نوح: عن الجريري، عن أبي العلاء، عن عثمان بن أبي العاص:
That he sent young slaves of his as traders, and when they came, he said: What have you brought?
They said: We have come with merchandise on which a dirham earns ten.
He said: And what is it?
They said: Wine.
He said: Wine, when we have been forbidden to drink it and to sell it?!
So he began opening the mouths of the wineskins and pouring it out (2) .
يونس بن عبيد: عن الحسن، عن عثمان بن أبي العاص ... , and he mentioned it similarly.
He died (may Allah be pleased with him): in the year 51.

174.h: 79 - ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih ibn Thaʿlabah al-Anṣārī * (4)
174.t:
al-Khazrajī, al-Madanī, the Badrī (البدري), one of the masters of ⟦2:375⟧ the Companions (الصحابي).
He witnessed: al-ʿAqabah, and Badr, and he is the one who was shown the call to prayer (1) , and that was in the first year of the Hijrah.
He has a few hadiths, and his hadith is in the Four Sunan collections (السنن).
It is said: the mention of Thaʿlabah in his lineage is a mistake.
Narrating from him: سعيد بن المسيب، وعبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى - and he did not meet him - ومحمد بن عبد الله ولده.
He died: in the year 32.
إسحاق الفروي: حدثنا عبد الله بن عمر العمري، عن بشر بن محمد بن عبد الله بن زيد، قال:
I came to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, and said: O Commander of the Faithful (أمير المؤمنين)! I am the son of the man of al-ʿAqabah and Badr, and the son of the one who was shown the call.
ʿUmar said: O people of Syria:
These are the noble deeds, not two cups of milk ... mixed with water, which afterwards turned to urine (2) ⟦2:376⟧
الأعمش: عن عمرو بن مرة، عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، قال:
The Companions (الصحابي) of Muḥammad ﷺ narrated to us:
That ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah! I saw in a dream a man standing on the stump of a wall, who called the adhān in pairs, and the iqāmah in pairs, and sat a sitting, and he wore two green cloaks (1) .
As for:

175.h: 80 - ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd ibn ʿĀṣim ibn Kaʿb al-Māzinī * (ع)
175.t:
al-Najjārī, the narrator of the hadith of ablution (2) , he was among the virtuous of the Companions (الصحابي).
He is known as: Ibn Umm ʿUmārah, and he is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd ibn ʿĀṣim ibn Kaʿb, of Banū Māzin ibn al-Najjār. ⟦2:377⟧
Ibn Mandah alone mentioned that he was a Badrī (البدري) (1) .
Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr and others said: Rather he was one of those at Uḥud (2) .
He is the one who killed Musaylimah with the sword, together with Waḥshī's throwing his spear at him (3) .
He is the paternal uncle of ʿAbbād ibn Tamīm.
It is said: he was killed on the day of al-Ḥarrah, in the year 63 (4) .

176.h: 81 - Ḥārithah ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn Nafʿ ibn Zayd ibn ʿUbayd al-Khazrajī *
176.t:
Ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Ghanm ibn Mālik ibn al-Najjār al-Khazrajī, al-Najjārī.
It is said: Ibn Rāfiʿ instead of Ibn Nafʿ.
His children were: ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Sawdah, ʿAmrah, and Umm Kulthūm.
His patronymic (الكنية) was Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
He witnessed Badr and the battles, and we do not know of any transmission from him; he was religious, good, and dutiful to his mother.
And from him, he said: I saw Jibrīl twice in all time: on the day of al-Ṣūrayn (5) when ⟦2:378⟧
the Messenger of Allah went out to Banū Qurayẓah, he passed by us in the form of Diḥyah, and commanded us to put on arms, and on the day at the place of the funerals when we returned from Ḥunayn, I passed while he was speaking with the Prophet ﷺ, and I did not give greeting.
Jibrīl said: Who is this, O Muḥammad?
He said: Ḥārithah ibn al-Nuʿmān.
He said: He is of the hundred steadfast on the day of Ḥunayn for whose provisions in Paradise Allah took charge, and had he given greeting, we would have returned it to him (1) .
It is narrated with a disconnected (المنقطع) chain of transmission (الإسناد): that Ḥārithah went blind, so he made a string from his place of prayer to his room, and put by him a basket containing dates and other things, and when a poor person gave greeting, he gave him from it, then took hold of the string until he came to the door of the room, and handed it to the poor person, and his family would say: We will suffice you. He would say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (Handing to the poor person protects against an evil death) (2) . ⟦2:379⟧
al-Wāqidī said: He had houses near the houses of the Prophet ﷺ, and whenever the Messenger of Allah took a new wife, Ḥārithah moved away from a house for him, until he said: (I have felt shame before Ḥārithah at his moving away from his houses for us (1)) .
He remained until the caliphate (الخلافة) of Muʿāwiyah.
Among his descendants: the hadith scholar (المحدث) Abū al-Rijāl Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥārithah ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Anṣārī, son of ʿAmrah the jurist (الفقيه) (2) .
And he - I mean Ḥārithah - is the one of whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (I entered Paradise, and heard recitation, and said: Who is this?
It was said: Ḥārithah.
The Prophet ﷺ said: Such is righteousness.)
He was dutiful to his mother (may Allah be pleased with him) (3) .
